## **Task 1: Creating DAX Measures**

DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) is the formula language of Power BI, similar to Excel formulas. In this lab you only need a handful of simple functions.

### **Column vs measure vs aggregation**

|   | What it is | When it is calculated | Example |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Column** (calculated column) | A new column added to a table; it has a value for every row | Once, when the data is loaded; stored in the file | Profit per Unit for each order line |
| **Aggregation** | A summary (Sum, Average, Count…) that Power BI applies automatically when you drop a numeric field in a visual | Each time the visual is drawn | “Sum of Sales” |
| **Measure** | A named DAX formula that you write once and reuse in any visual | Dynamically, every time a filter or slicer changes | Total Sales \= SUM(Sales\[Sales\]) |

 

In a formula, a column is written as TableName\[ColumnName\], for example Sales\[Profit\]. A measure is written in square brackets only, for example \[Total Profit\].

### **1 Create your first measure**

1\. In the Report **view**, click the **Sales** table in the Data pane (a measure is stored in a table; we place all measures in Sales).

2\. On the **Home** tab, click **New measure**. The formula bar opens.

3\. Replace the text with the formula below and press **Enter**.

Total Sales \= SUM(Sales\[Sales\])

4\. The measure appears in the Sales table with a calculator icon. With it selected, use **Measure tools → Format**: Format **Decimal number**, **2** decimal places, thousands separator **On**.

### **2 Create the remaining measures**

Repeat the steps (select Sales → New measure → type → Enter → format) for each of the following.

| Measure | DAX formula | Format |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Total Profit | Total Profit \= SUM(Sales\[Profit\]) | Decimal, 2 places |
| Total Quantity | Total Quantity \= SUM(Sales\[Quantity\]) | Whole number, thousands separator |
| Total Orders | Total Orders \= DISTINCTCOUNT(Sales\[OrderID\]) | Whole number |
| Average Order Value | Average Order Value \= DIVIDE(\[Total Sales\], \[Total Orders\]) | Decimal, 2 places |
| Profit Margin | Profit Margin \= DIVIDE(\[Total Profit\], \[Total Sales\]) | **Percentage**, 2 places |

 

### **3  Use the measures in your visuals**

1\. Select the card from Visualization 1\. In the **Visualizations** pane, remove **Sum of Sales** from **Fields** (click ✕) and drag the measure **Total Sales** in its place. The number must stay the same.

2\. Replace **Sum of Sales** with **Total Sales** in Visualizations 2, 3 and 4, and **Sum of Profit** with **Total Profit** in Visualization 5\. The charts should not change.

3\. Add three more **Card** visuals showing **Total Profit**, **Profit Margin** and **Average Order Value**. Use the Format settings from Visualization 1 (title, display units None). For Profit Margin the card should show a percentage.

4\. Add a **Table** visual with these fields: **Dim\_Product\[Category\]**, **Total Sales**, **Total Profit**, **Profit Margin**. This is your category summary table.

5\. Add a **Clustered bar chart**: **Y-axis \= Dim\_Product\[Product\]**, **X-axis \= Profit Margin**. Sort ascending by Profit Margin so the least profitable product is at the top. Title it Profit Margin by Product.

### **4  Experiment: calculated column vs measure**

You will see for yourself why a measure is often the right choice.

1\. Select the **Sales** table and click **Table tools → New column** (or the **Modeling** tab). Enter:

Profit per Unit \= DIVIDE(Sales\[Profit\], Sales\[Quantity\])

2\. In the Data pane drag **Profit per Unit** into a temporary Card. Change its aggregation to **Average** (click the ▼ beside the field name in the Fields well → **Average**).

3\. Create the measure below and show it in a second temporary card:

Average Profit per Unit \= DIVIDE(\[Total Profit\], \[Total Quantity\])

4\. Compare the two numbers. Then delete both temporary cards (the column and measure may stay in the model).

### **Questions**

| \# | Question | Your answer |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 5.1 | Record the value of each measure: Total Sales, Total Profit, Total Quantity, Total Orders, Average Order Value, Profit Margin. |   |
| 5.2 | Which category has the lowest **Profit Margin** in your category summary table? What is its margin? |   |
| 5.3 | In Step 4, what values did the two temporary cards show? Why are they different? (Hint: one is an average of 200 row-level ratios, the other is total profit divided by total units.) |   |

 

## **Task 2 Filters and Slicers**

Interactivity lets the person reading your report ask their own questions. Power BI offers four related tools:

| Tool | Applies to | Who controls it? | Where |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Slicer** | Any visuals on the page it is connected to | The report reader, by clicking | A visual on the canvas |
| **Visual-level filter** | One selected visual only | The report author (reader can see it) | Filters pane → “Filters on this visual” |
| **Page-level filter** | All visuals on one page | The report author | Filters pane → “Filters on this page” |
| **Report-level filter** | All visuals on every page | The report author | Filters pane → “Filters on all pages” |

 

Besides slicers and filters, clicking a bar or a point in one visual **cross-filters** the other visuals on the page. Click an empty area of the visual (or the same bar again) to clear the selection.

### **1  Add four slicers**

1\. Click an empty area of the canvas. In the Visualizations pane select the **Slicer** icon.

2\. Drag **Dim\_Region\[Region\]** into **Field**. Format visual → **Slicer settings → Options → Style: Tile** (buttons). Title: Region.

3\. Add a second slicer with **Dim\_Product\[Category\]**, style **Tile** or **Dropdown**. Title: Category.

4\. Add a third slicer with **Sales\[Customer Segment\]**, style **Tile**. Title: Customer Segment.

5\. Add a fourth slicer with **Dim\_Date\[Date\]**. Format visual → **Slicer settings → Options → Style: Between**. This gives a date-range slider. Title: Order Date.

6\. Test: click “East” in the Region slicer. All visuals update. Hold **Ctrl** and click a second region to select several. Click the eraser icon (top-right of the slicer) to clear.

### **2 Investigate with the slicers**

Use the slicers to answer these questions. Clear the slicers between questions.

### **3 Practise the three filter levels**

To avoid damaging your dashboard page, practise on a copy.

1\. Right-click the page tab → **Duplicate page**. Rename the copy Filter Practice. (Or add a new page and copy-paste visuals into it with Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V.)

**2\. Visual-level filter:** on the Filter Practice page select the \*Profit Margin by Product\* bar chart. In the **Filters pane**, under **Filters on this visual**, hover over **Product** → expand → set **Filter type: Top N**, **Show items: Bottom 3**, **By value: Profit Margin** → **Apply filter**. Record the three products.

**3\. Page-level filter:** click an empty area of the page so no visual is selected. Drag **Sales\[Customer Segment\]** into **Filters on this page**, tick **Corporate**. Record the Total Sales card value for this page.

**4\. Report-level filter:** drag **Sales\[Payment Method\]** into **Filters on all pages**, tick **Credit Card**. Record the Total Sales card value now. Then switch to your dashboard page: what happened there?

5\. Remove the report-level filter (click the eraser/✕ beside it) so the dashboard page returns to normal. You may delete the Filter Practice page afterwards.

## **Task 3 Building an Interactive Dashboard**

A good dashboard answers a question at a glance. Now arrange the visuals you have already built into one professional report page called **Retail Sales Dashboard**.

### **Design guidelines**

**•** **Avoid unnecessary visuals.** Every visual must answer a business question.

**•** **Use meaningful titles** that say what is shown (“Total Sales by Region”, not “Chart 3”).

**•** **Keep formatting consistent:** same font, same title size, same alignment, same number formats.

**•** **Avoid excessive colours.** Use one main colour (for example dark blue) and one accent colour. Colours should carry meaning, not decoration.

**•** **Make KPIs easy to see:** put them in a row at the top, large and clearly labelled.

**•** **Arrange visuals logically:** overview at the top (KPIs), then trend, then breakdowns; slicers together on the left or top.

**•** **Do not overcrowd.** Leave small gaps between visuals; align edges.

### **Required content**

| Element | Visual to include |
| :---- | :---- |
| Report title | A text box with the report title |
| KPI cards | Total Sales, Total Profit, Profit Margin, Average Order Value |
| Sales trend | Line chart: Total Sales by Month |
| Category analysis | Column chart: Total Sales by Category |
| Regional analysis | Bar chart: Total Sales by Region |
| Profit analysis | Column chart: Total Profit by Category (and the Profit Margin by Product bar chart) |
| Slicers | Region, Category, Customer Segment, Order Date (at least two required; use all four) |

 

### **Suggested layout (canvas 1280 × 720\)**

![][image1]

 

| Visual | X | Y | Width | Height |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Title text box (dark background) | 0 | 0 | 1280 | 70 |
| Slicers: Region / Category / Customer Segment / Date | 20 | 90 / 235 / 380 / 510 | 210 | 135 / 135 / 120 / 110 |
| KPI cards (4) | 250, 506, 762, 1018 | 85 | 240 | 90 |
| Line chart: Monthly Sales Trend | 250 | 190 | 620 | 250 |
| Column chart: Sales by Category | 886 | 190 | 372 | 250 |
| Bar chart: Sales by Region | 250 | 455 | 330 | 250 |
| Column chart: Profit by Category | 596 | 455 | 330 | 250 |
| Bar chart: Profit Margin by Product | 942 | 455 | 316 | 250 |

 

### **Steps**

1\. Select a visual, open **Format visual → General → Properties → Size / Position** and type the X, Y, Width and Height values. (You may also drag visuals by eye if you prefer, but align the edges using **Format → Align**.)

2\. Add the title: **Insert → Text box**. Type Retail Sales Performance Dashboard  2025. Make it bold, size 24; give it a dark blue background and white text.

3\. Choose a consistent look: **View → Themes** and pick one theme, then set every title to the same font size (for example 14\) and alignment.

4\. Click on a bar in the Category chart and check that the other visuals filter. Use **Format → Edit interactions** if any visual (for example the KPI cards) behaves unexpectedly.

5\. Clear all slicers and selections so that the report opens showing overall totals.

6\. Save the report (**Ctrl \+ S**).
